newsitem.title: UK: UK postpones tax self-assessment for companies.
newsitem.headline: UK postpones tax self-assessment for companies.

text.p: Britain has postponed the introduction of tax self-assessment for companies until early 1999 at the earliest.
The Inland Revenue had initially assumed that the appointed day would be for accounting periods ending on or after March 31, 1998.
The later start date for companies will allow Corporation Tax Pay and File, a system introduced in 1993, more time for preparation, the Inland Revenue said.
For personal taxpayers -- individuals, partnerships and trustees -- the first year of self-assessment is fiscal 1996/97. -- London Newsroom +44 171 542 7717
